description:
FILED s463av.  #950 asked for the (speed 3) note harvest as a BUG FINDER — the
`%p-fixnum-string` generic-TRUNCATE class (#922) was invisible at the default
policy and loud at speed 3 — so here is the census it produced, and what is
left in it after s463av took the two findings it could.

HOW TO REPRODUCE.  `load` of a source file does NOT emit optimization notes, so
the harvest is a COMPILE-FILE in an image that has already loaded the runtime
(the runtime sets `(readtable-case *readtable*) :invert` and `require`s
cl-ppcre / sb-posix mid-file, so compile-file on a cold image reads garbage):

    (let ((*error-output* (make-broadcast-stream)))
      (handler-bind ((warning #'muffle-warning)) (load "cl/pcl-runtime.lisp")))
    (proclaim '(optimize (speed 3)))
    (handler-bind ((warning #'muffle-warning))
      (compile-file "cl/pcl-runtime.lisp" :output-file "/tmp/x.fasl"))

THE CENSUS (3179 notes, s463av tree).  By class:

    1528  unable to optimize (type uncertainty, mostly REAL-vs-float)
     424  unable to open-code FLOAT to RATIONAL comparison
     224  unable to avoid runtime dispatch on array element type (hairy aref)
     248  unable to optimize away possible call to FDEFINITION   <- CLOSED, see below
     130  forced to do generic-+        63  generic--     59  <-integer-fixnum
      57  forced to do full call        55  SAP to pointer coercion
      54  generic-<   41  generic->     31  generic-*   14  generic-=
      13  generic-negate                24+21 upgraded-element-type unknown

By function (top):

     162  set-capture-groups        102  p-dualvar         74  p-sprintf
      72  sprintf-one                60  %pcl-days-to-ymd  58  %p-open-parse-2arg
      53  (setf p-errno-string)      51  unbox             42  sprintf-format-float-e
      42  do-regex-match             38  p-split           38  %pcl-scan-anchored-list
      35  set-match-vars             33  %p-parse-require-version
      32  parse-perl-number          26  %p-local-array-slice-nested

THE READING THAT MATTERS, AND IT IS GOOD NEWS: the HOT element and loop paths
are NOT at the top.  `p-aref`, `(setf p-aref)`, `%p-aref-store`, `%p-vpush`,
`p-+` carry only a handful of notes each, and every one of them sits in the
GENERAL fallback arm — the fast arms added by s458ak (#815/#811) and s462as
(#923) are already open-coded, and the notes are the price of the fallback
existing at all.  A note is not a cost until something takes that arm.

WHAT s463av TOOK:
  * the 248 FDEFINITION notes — ALL of them one missing declaration.  Every one
    is `(funcall (p-magic-cell-getter v))`, inlined into `unbox` / `box-set` /
    `p-dualvar` / `(setf p-errno-string)`.  All eleven `make-p-magic-cell` call
    sites pass functions, so the slots are now `:type function` with erroring
    defaults (rule 12).  Cold path, so no measurable speed change — it is a
    declared invariant and 8 % of the census gone.
  * the extension-stub self-call, task #980 — the harvest's real bug, and it
    was found by RUNNING at speed 3 rather than by reading a note.

WHAT IS LEFT, in the order a future session should look at it:

 1. THE REGEX CAPTURE PATH — 239 notes across `set-capture-groups` (162, of
    which 45 are hairy-aref), `set-match-vars` (35) and `do-regex-match` (42).
    That is the largest single concentration in the file and it is on the
    per-MATCH path, which #680 has already shown is where regex time goes.  The
    hairy-aref notes say the capture vectors' element type is unknown at every
    access — the same shape `%p-vec-data` fixed for arrays (s458ak) and
    `%p-flatten-list` fixed for the flattener (#923).  NOT taken in s463av:
    `do-regex-match` / `do-regex-subst` belonged to the sibling agent that
    round.  Do this one WITH a profile (`regexg` row), not from the notes.

 2. THE FLOAT-vs-RATIONAL class (424) — `p-sprintf` 18, `sprintf-one` 16,
    `p-require-version` 14, `%p-true-p-slow` 12, the `%def-overloaded-cmp`
    family 12 each.  These are comparisons of a value typed REAL against a
    literal, where SBCL must go through a rational contagion path.  Cheap to
    test on one function; measure before spreading.

 3. `%pcl-days-to-ymd` (60) / `%pcl-unix-to-utc` (24) — pure integer date
    arithmetic doing GENERIC +, -, *.  Isolated, self-contained, and the values
    are provably fixnums; the smallest safe declaration exercise in the file.
    Worth it only if a profile ever puts localtime/gmtime on a hot path.

 4. `%p-open-parse-2arg` (58) and `parse-perl-number` (32) — string walking with
    unknown element types.  Per-open and per-numification, not per-element.

NOT A TODO LIST.  A note is evidence, not a cost: item 1 has a profile behind it
and the rest do not.  The one thing this census IS good for unchanged is
RE-RUNNING it after a change — a new concentration in a hot function is the
signal #922 was.
subject: The (speed 3) optimization-note census: 3179 notes, and 239 of them are on the regex capture path (set-capture-groups / set-match-vars / do-regex-match)
